lanes.hillsLocal.note: Eric, 2026-10-31: almost every hill street is two lanes, one each direction. Applied to Local streets in City Fire Zones 2 and 3.

lanes.byClass.note: Total lanes by County CLASS where the City pavement-management lane count is missing.

parking.hills.note: Status quo in Fire Zones 2–3: residents would park on both sides (Eric, 2026-10-31), but each run draws one side only on some blocks (parking.range). The City's curb data or aerial counts would replace this.

parking.flats.note: Placeholder: parking on both sides. Replace with the City's curb data.

parking.parkedCarWidthM.note: 8 ft per parked side, as used by KLD in the SB 99 and AB 747 analyses (SOURCE_NOTES A1).

capacity.speedMph.note: Free-flow speed by road class (hills 20 mph matches AB 747: hills free flow 20 mph or less). Capped by the City network SPEED where known. Replace with KLD's surveyed speeds.

capacity.twoLanePcphPerMph.note: AB 747 Table 2 (HCM 2022): two-lane road capacity = 45 pc/h per mph of free-flow speed, max 1,700 (SOURCE_NOTES B2). Applied per direction.

capacity.multilanePcphPerLane.note: AB 747: 1,900 pc/h per lane for multilane roadways (SOURCE_NOTES B3).

capacity.freewayPcphPerLane.note: AB 747: 2,250 pc/h per lane for freeways at 55 mph (SOURCE_NOTES B3).

capacity.rampPcphPerLane.note: Ramp capacity placeholder; AB 747 uses HCM Exhibit 14-12 by ramp speed.

capacity.steepFactor.note: Flow multiplier on segments whose steep grade (90th percentile of 25 m windows) exceeds steepGradePct. KLD's surveyed speeds would already include grade.

capacity.vehicleSpacingM.note: Road length one queued vehicle occupies (storage).

access.movingLaneM.note: 10 ft minimum viable evacuation travel lane, chosen by KLD with City Public Works and Fire staff (SOURCE_NOTES A2).

access.engineClearM.note: Largest City fire truck is 9.25 ft wide (SB 99 report, SOURCE_NOTES A3); with mirrors it needs the same 10 ft lane.

access.fireCodeClearM.note: 20 ft unobstructed width for fire apparatus access roads, California Fire Code section 503.2.1. Context only: it governs new access roads, not existing streets.

access.engineServiceMin.note: 5-minute fire-station drive-time standard from the City's Standards of Coverage, as used in the SB 99 analysis (SOURCE_NOTES A6).

intersections.note: Total vehicles per hour a node can pass, by the highest road class meeting there. Illustrative. The 2025 study names intersections as the main constraint.

demand.personsPerHousehold.note: 2.37 persons per household (ACS), Evacuation Time Study 2-1, 3-3 (SOURCE_NOTES E5). Converts Genasys zone population estimates to households.

demand.householdsWithoutVehicleShare.note: 7.47% of households have no vehicle (ACS), Time Study Table 3-10 (SOURCE_NOTES E7). Citywide value; AB 747 has it by census tract.

demand.vehiclesTakenShares.note: Of households that drive: 1 vehicle 73.6%, 2 vehicles 14.6%, 3 vehicles 1.3%, 4+ 0.5% (Time Study survey, Fig. D-11), renormalized (SOURCE_NOTES E6).

demand.carlessRideshareShare.note: 86.9% of people without a vehicle ride with someone else (Time Study 3-9). In the simulator they ride with an evacuating household on the same street; the rest are stranded (SOURCE_NOTES E7).

demand.compliance.note: Share of households that leave: 100% in Order zones, 50% in Warning zones, 20% shadow/voluntary elsewhere (Time Study 2-3, 7-1, from NUREG/CR-7002) (SOURCE_NOTES E8). Shadow evacuees drive to the city edge.

demand.childPickupShare.note: Share of households that pick up children when school is in session (switches to Time Study distributions E/F). Placeholder; ACS households with children would replace it.

demand.mobilization15min.note: Percent of trips starting in each 15-minute period after the order, Time Study Table 5-9 (p. 5-14) (SOURCE_NOTES E9). A employees/visitors; C residents awaiting a returning commuter (also used for shadow evacuees); D residents not awaiting one; E/F = C/D with child pickup.

parking.range.note: Parking varies by block and by seed. On hill blocks wide enough for both sides: noParkingShareHills parked on neither side, oneSideShareHills on one side, the rest on both (City 2020 aerial counts of 22 hill blocks, data/field/aerial-parking-counts-2020.json: of 12 wider blocks 2 had none, 4 one side, 6 both on at least part; on blocks of 22 ft or less 7 of 9 were one side or sparse, which the 8 ft rule below already produces). offPavementShare / offPavementSavesM: share of hill blocks where cars sit partly off the pavement and the width that saves (Poppy Ln, Latham Ln photos). minLeftForCarsM: residents stop parking where less than 8 ft would remain for a car (City Narrow_Roads shows 7-8 ft left on many streets). curbMPerCar: one parked car per this many meters of a parked side (aerial counts: about 19 m in daytime; 15 assumed to allow for fuller evenings). badJobPerCar, badJobExtraM: each parked car has a small chance of being a bad job (wide vehicle or far from the curb) that narrows the gap by 1.5-4 ft (red van photo); not measurable from the aerials. Placeholders until curb data or evening counts.

sharedLane.note: Two-way streets with one moving lane between parked cars: both directions share one lane's capacity. When both directions have traffic, drivers take turns at gaps (driveways) every passingGapM; each switch loses about passingGapM / speed + 3 s against platoonS of flow. Below one 10 ft lane flow is cut by squeezeBelowLaneFactor; below crawlBelowM (7 ft) cars creep through at crawlFactor. Placeholders until gap spacing is counted from aerial photos. opposingWaitS: in route choice, each oncoming car on a one-lane street counts as this much delay, so drivers avoid turning into oncoming traffic (without it, re-routing around hill loops created two-way jams on Panoramic Hill).

demand.returnDriveMin.note: Households awaiting a returning commuter (Time Study distributions C and E): the commuter leaves work on the Time Study employee curve (Table 5-9 A), then drives this many minutes (uniform range) to reach the edge of the evacuating area, then drives home on Berkeley streets against the outbound traffic. Their car is one of the household's vehicles, so it adds an inbound trip but no extra outbound vehicle. A commuter turned back by fire leaves the household one car short. Workplace locations are not modeled.

capacity.gridlockReliefS.note: A vehicle that has waited this long at the head of a queue squeezes into a full downstream link, and an oncoming car stuck this long no longer holds up the other direction on a take-turns street. Prevents permanent lock-ups that a simple queue model creates in rings such as traffic circles. Each use is counted in the run summary.

nonResident.note: Vehicle counts from the 2025 Evacuation Time Study: employees by area (Table 3-5), college students (Tables 3-8, 3-9), visitors including 549 at Tilden lots (§3.5), I-80 through traffic over 2 h after the order (Table 3-12); scaled by the scenario's percent present (Table 6-5) (SOURCE_NOTES E32-E36). Placement is a model rule: the study's areas are approximated from City neighborhoods (West Berkeley = 4th St., Gilman, NW/SW Berkeley, Marina), fire zones (hills north/south of campus), LBNL employees on streets in the Lab's zones (LBL-*), 400 m around Berkeley City College, streets within 1 km of the campus center, outside the campus and outside Fire Zones 2-3, for commuting students; visitors on streets outside Fire Zones 2-3, 400 m around two Tilden entrances (approximate points), weighted by street length. The I-80 and CA-24 westbound (the study's "SB") parts of the study's through traffic are on our network; I-580 and I-880 lie outside the model area except where I-580 shares the I-80 freeway.

intersections.delayS.note: Average delay per junction when traffic is light, added to the travel time into each junction: about 20 s at arterial junctions (mostly signals; HCM uncongested signal delay is typically 10-35 s), 10 s on collectors, 5 s on local streets (stop signs, yielding). The street file has no signal or stop-sign data; the Time Study models each signal. Set once from typical values, not tuned.

intersections.scale.note: Multiplier on collector and arterial intersection capacities (local and freeway junctions unchanged). The one setting tuned against the Time Study (1923 repeat, night S3 and fall weekday S4); checked on cases not used for tuning. See SOURCE_NOTES calibration.

parking.range.night.note: Night cases (Time Study S3, S6): residents are home, so fewer hill blocks have no parked cars and parked sides are fuller (one car per 9 m instead of 15 m), which raises the chance of a bad parking job. Placeholder until evening counts or curb data; daytime aerial counts found about one car per 19 m. Suggested in pasted egress notes (SOURCE_NOTES P3) and consistent with Eric's photos being daytime.

intersections.circleVph.note: Traffic circles at about 900 veh/h per lane (Time Study Appendix G, SOURCE_NOTES E16), applied to network nodes inside OpenStreetMap junction=roundabout rings.

access.barrierDelayS.note: Time for an engine crew to open a gate or remove an emergency bollard (3 min, middle of the 2-5 min in pasted egress notes, SOURCE_NOTES P2; unsourced).

population.overrides.note: Eric, 2026-11-01: OKL-003 (Claremont Canyon, an R04 Panoramic Hill order zone) uses the 2020 Census count (307 people in the blocks whose interior point lies in the zone; Census TIGERweb, POP100) instead of the Genasys estimate (27). Per zone: "census2020" replaces the Genasys estimate with the Census count. SOURCE_NOTES X6.

network.segmentCorrections.note: County street-file records corrected where other sources agree the County coding is wrong; each is matched by SEGID and OBJECTID, sets the listed County fields before the network is built, and is listed in network.meta.segmentCorrections and on the edge (correction). Eric, 2026-11-01: the 45 m link from the foot of Panoramic Way to Prospect St / Canyon Rd (County OBJECTID 25386, SEGID 181025458, "BANCROFT STEPS WY", TRVLWAY NT) is a two-way street. OpenStreetMap maps it as Bancroft Way (way 24025453, highway=tertiary, lanes=2, no access or oneway tags, checked 2026-11-01); the City Street_Centerline layer has it as pavement section 627042086 (Seg-00193, Prospect St to Panoramic Way, 30 ft, 2 lanes, two-way); the City's AB 747 street layer gives it a capacity of 1,125 vehicles/h; the SB 99 report (KLD, Rev. 3, p. 4) puts Panoramic Hill's single access point at "Panoramic Way and Prospect St/Canyon Rd". The Bancroft Steps stairway is a separate feature (OSM ways 311861379-311861382 and 24025452, motor_vehicle=no, Warring St to Prospect St) and is not in the County file. SOURCE_NOTES K1-K6.

segmentCorrections.why: Drivable two-way link from the foot of Panoramic Way to Prospect St / Canyon Rd, Panoramic Hill's single exit (SB 99, p. 4). OSM: Bancroft Way, tertiary, 2 lanes, no access restriction; City Street_Centerline Seg-00193: 30 ft, 2 lanes, two-way. The County record codes it no vehicle travel and names it after the Bancroft Steps stairway, which runs from Warring St to Prospect St and is a separate feature.
